featured_reviews.name: Fizza Ratlamwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Megumi recently and had a really enjoyable dining experience. The space feels refined and calm, with a warm, premium vibe that makes you want to slow down and enjoy the meal. Service was attentive without being intrusive and everything arrived on time and was explained well.

The food truly stood out. The salmon truffle cream cheese was smooth, rich and beautifully balanced, with the truffle adding depth without overpowering the dish. The chargrilled chicken was juicy and nicely smoked, cooked just right.

The kimchi fried rice was flavour-packed with a perfect tangy kick, and adding chicken made it even more satisfying. Some of the more subtle dishes brought in great umami flavours and variety, making the overall meal feel well thought out.

Desserts were a highlight. The bitter chocolate mousse was indulgent yet not overly sweet, and the Japanese honey cheesecake was light, soft and the perfect way to end the meal.

Overall, Megumi delivers on flavours, presentation and service. A great choice for a relaxed yet elevated dining experience, whether it’s a special outing or a quiet evening out.

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Sanghvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Megumi is a beautiful place for candel light dinner with your loved ones. As the name suggests it has a curated menu with Japanese delicacies and has a perfect romantic vibe. I visited with my partner for our Anniversary Celebration and we loved the experience.

🧆FOOD: Entire menu has a variety of Japanese dishes way more than Sushi and Dimsums. We tried Cottage Cheese Kung Pao, Open Sushi and Enoki Sushi. Another unique dish which we tried was Mushroom Gyoza which are like half fired and half steamed Dimsums along with Kimchi Rice in staples. We also tried the bar tender recommend Cocktails 🍸which were really crazy. For Desserts I tried the Bitter Chocolate Mousse which I will highly recommend for dark chocolate lovers.

🎭 AMBIENCE: It's on the top floor of the building and asthetic Japanese themed decor, high roof and romantic lights. Perfect mood setter for a special occasion and ample seating space available. Service was also fine with corporative staff.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Some restaurants get the ambiance right.
Some focus entirely on the food.
And then there are places like Megumi that manage to do both beautifully.

From the moment we walked in, the space felt warm, elegant, and calming without trying too hard. The kind of restaurant where you instantly know you’re going to enjoy spending time — whether it’s for a quiet dinner, a catch-up with friends, or simply a slow evening over good food.

The meal began with complimentary sweet potato chips served alongside a jalapeño dip and chilli oil, and honestly, this small opening already set the tone for the evening. Crisp, addictive, and paired with dips that added both heat and freshness — it was one of those thoughtful touches that immediately makes you feel taken care of.

We then moved on to the Daikon Cake, which was beautifully executed with a lovely balance of texture and flavour. Comforting, delicate, and packed with umami, it was the kind of dish that quietly impresses you.

The Spicy Corn Curd was another standout for me. Creamy, flavourful, and carrying just the right amount of spice, it struck that perfect balance between indulgent and light. Definitely one of those dishes I’d happily reorder.

But the real star of the meal was the Edamame and Truffle Fried Rice. Fragrant, comforting, and deeply satisfying, this dish had everything working in its favour. The truffle flavour was present without overpowering the dish, while the edamame added texture and freshness. Easily one of the best things we ate that evening.

We also tried the Smoked Cottage Cheese Robata, which brought in beautiful smoky flavours while still letting the softness of the cottage cheese shine through. Rich, well-balanced, and very satisfying.

To end the meal, we had the Almond Coffee Delicai, which was smooth, indulgent, and the perfect finish to the evening. The coffee and almond combination worked beautifully together without feeling too heavy.

Final thoughts:
Megumi delivers exactly what you hope for from a good Asian dining experience — thoughtful food, balanced flavours, warm hospitality, and an ambiance that makes you want to stay longer. Every dish felt carefully crafted, and the overall meal struck that lovely balance between comfort and elegance.

A beautiful dining experience in Santacruz that I’d happily go back to. ✨

featured_reviews.name: Sunny Gurnani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sea princess, a renowned hotel in Juhu from years now which is known for its hospitality came up with this restaurant Jeon on its ground floor and gave an opportunity to people other than their Inhouse guests too to experience this lavish restaurant serving many of the delicious items with their wide ranged buffet menu. Right from the entrance upto the exit, everything was a nice experience.

The place is very well designed keeping many things in mind. The seating is very comfortable and spacious unlike we often experience at buffet place. The price of 1600 INR for the weekday dinner gets you a full fledged meal from soups, chaat counter, salad bar, live pasta and delicacies from North India, mughlai and Asia.

Non-veg Starters had chicken cajun which had tender chicken well greased and tossed to crisp and tawa fry basa which is barely found anywhere coz basa is soft and people find it real hard to tawa fry such soft fish but here at Jeon, It wasn't just tawa fried but was fried to perfection with right marination making it all the more Delicious.

Veg starters: veg crispy and paneer tikka which was fresh and soft very well marinated and grilled. It went well with the chutney served alongside

Loved pani puri served here with options to select from ragda or potato and sprouts.

Salad bar options can get better with more choices of essentials for health freaks.

The Chef at pasta counter made us a white sauce pasta which was super yum. Specially the bread severs with it was too good.

Mains: A wide spread counter focusing on mains unlike other bunches I have attended recently where their focus is Mainly on starters. Their dal makhani Cannot be missed. Mutton rara was something I couldn't hold onto after first bite. It was lamb cooked at its best and softness. They had items to suit all taste buds from domestic to international.

Desserts : someone who designer the buffet menu at Jeon must be dessert lover for they have given special attention to the desssert counter which was surprisingly bigger than the main course counter with so many options for anyone to go Gaga. While it's practically impossible to try so many items, some of what I witnessed here was blueberry pie, apple streusel, sago pudding, choclate orange marmalade, carrot cake, dual pannacotta, strawberry jelly, and some more.

It was indeed an amazing experience we here for our dinner here. I wish if the dinner buffet could have included a drink or a cocktail too and also the manager who came lil rude to us which could be just one of the bad days for him however it's a place you must visit for its everyday changing menu when the chef is up to make something out of the set menu too if hour wish to.

Dynasty: The Indo-Chinese Restaurant That Doesn’t Need Buzz
Five stars aren’t enough, but they’ll have to do.
Dynasty operates in that rare territory where quality speaks louder than Instagram followers. This unpretentious neighborhood spot has mastered the art of authentic Indo-Chinese cooking — the kind that requires skill, not shortcuts.
Order the Chicken Lollipop and you’ll understand immediately. Each piece is a study in balance: crisp exterior, succulent interior, perfectly seasoned. The Manchow Soup arrives with the kind of umami depth that makes you wonder why other restaurants even bother. The Crispy Spinach Chicken demands respect, while the Crispy Thread Chicken delivers texture with purpose. These aren’t interpretations — they’re the genuine article.
But the real revelation lies in the Sour Chili and Sichuan dips. Layered, bold, and unapologetically complex, they’re the kind of accompaniments that transform a meal into an experience. The lemon iced tea cuts through it all with perfect timing.
What distinguishes Dynasty, though, is the service. The team moves with purpose, never intrusive, always present. It’s a family restaurant in the truest sense — one that makes you feel like you belong.
In a city saturated with forgettable Indo-Chinese, Dynasty reminds you why authenticity never goes out of style.

Dynasty Restaurant, Khar West: A Chinese Culinary Journey

Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West, Mumbai, is a haven for Chinese food enthusiasts. This popular eatery has been delighting taste buds with its authentic and flavorful dishes for years. Whether you're craving spicy, tangy, or sweet, Dynasty has something to offer.

One of the must-try dishes at Dynasty is their Crispy Spinach Paneer. This vegetarian delight features tender cubes of paneer coated in a crispy batter and tossed with fresh spinach. The combination of textures and flavors is simply irresistible. For a refreshing drink to complement your meal, try their Ice Lemon Tea. The tartness of the lemon combined with the sweetness of the tea makes it a perfect thirst quencher.

If you're looking for something spicy, the Paneer Chilli is a great option. Tender pieces of paneer are stir-fried with a spicy chili sauce, making it a fiery dish that will leave your taste buds tingling. For a unique twist on Chinese cuisine, try the Schezwan Crispy Veg. This dish features mixed vegetables coated in a crispy batter and tossed in a spicy Schezwan sauce.

For a satisfying main course, consider the Veg Burnt Garlic Rice or the Veg Malaysian Noodles. Both dishes are packed with flavor and are sure to leave you feeling full and satisfied. Dynasty also offers a variety of Indian Chinese dishes, combining traditional Indian flavors with Chinese cooking techniques.

To start your meal, the Manchow Soup is a classic choice. This flavorful soup is packed with vegetables and a hint of spice. For a refreshing and tangy drink, try the Sweet and Salty Lime Soda. The combination of sweet and salty flavors is a unique and refreshing treat.

Whether you're a seasoned Chinese food lover or new to the cuisine, Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West is a must-visit. With its delicious food, friendly service, and inviting atmosphere, it's no wonder why this restaurant is so popular among locals and tourists alike.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely Blown Away by Osttaad! ✨ (5/5 Stars)

Just experienced a truly exceptional meal at the newly opened @Osttaadmumbai in Santacruz West, and I'm still dreaming about the explosion of flavors! This place is a MUST-TRY for anyone looking for a unique and refined dining experience. The menu is a beautiful tapestry of Northwestern and Central Asian cuisine, and each dish we ordered was a masterpiece.

We started with the Spanakopita, which was perfectly flaky and filled with a delicious, savory spinach and feta mixture. A great light start to the meal.

Next up were the appetizers from the tandoor, and they were the stars of the show! The Murgh Pashtooni Sheek was incredibly tender and flavorful, with subtle hints of spices that left you wanting more. The Adana Kebab was another winner – perfectly grilled, juicy, and with a lovely smoky char. But the absolute standout was the Zafrani Tandoori Jhinga. The prawns were succulent and infused with a fragrant saffron marinade – truly divine!

For the mains, we opted for the classic Murgh Makhanwala, and Osttaad's rendition was rich, creamy, and utterly satisfying. It paired perfectly with the Butter Garlic Naan, which was soft, buttery, and garlicky in all the right ways.

To end the delightful meal, we indulged in the Baklava. It was perfectly sweet, nutty, and flaky – the ideal sweet conclusion.

Beyond the incredible food, the ambience at Osttaad is elegant and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a sophisticated night out. The service was also impeccable – attentive and knowledgeable.

Overall: Osttaad is a gem of a restaurant that brings a unique and exciting culinary experience to Mumbai. The quality of the food, the beautiful ambience, and the excellent service make it a top contender in the city's dining scene. I can't wait to visit again and explore more of their fascinating menu!

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Osttaad brings the vibrant flavors of Central Asia right to Santacruz West, Mumbai. Drawing inspiration from the rich culinary traditions of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Iran, China, and more, this restaurant offers a unique fusion that blends age-old heritage with a modern twist. Every dish is a journey through spice, culture, and story, thoughtfully reimagined for today’s palate.

The ambience is warm and inviting, with soulful interiors and aesthetic decor that make it a perfect spot to relax with your loved one or catch a vibe with friends. One of the standout design features is their stunning cave-shaped bar counter, adding a unique charm to the space.

We started our evening with two refreshing cocktails: the Sundown Silk, a gin-based cocktail that was light, aromatic, and incredibly refreshing; and the Emir Noir, a tequila-based drink that was bold, flavorful, and a total game changer. Both were absolute hits!

For starters, we tried the Murgh Pashtooni Seekh, which was juicy, tender, and packed with flavor. The Silky Mushroom Galawat, served with yogurt cream on a bed of khasta bread, was another favorite – rich, creamy, and full of texture. The Rashmi Murgh Malai Kebab was perfectly spiced and presented beautifully, and once again, loved by everyone at the table.

The highlight of the evening was the Murgh Parda Biryani – a chef’s special that you won’t find anywhere else in Mumbai. It was absolutely divine, with layers of flavor and a presentation that impressed. We also enjoyed the Murgh Shinwari, a mildly spiced chicken curry inspired by the Pashtun tribes, paired with freshly made tandoori roti. It was soulful and comforting.

To end on a sweet note, we indulged in a delicious Baklava – crisp, sweet, and the perfect finale to a flavorful meal.

Overall, our experience at Osttaad was a solid 10/10. From the food and drinks to the ambience and service, everything was top-notch. The staff was attentive, and the manager guided us through the menu with care and enthusiasm.

If you're in Santacruz West, Osttaad is a must-visit spot for a unique and memorable dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Purva Sangade
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked away in the heart of Santacruz, Osttaad is not just a restaurant — it’s a culinary passport to Central Asia. From the moment you step in, the ambience wraps you in a warm, earthy charm that blends tradition with a bold modern twist. The interiors are inviting, the vibe is soulful, and the food? Nothing short of unforgettable.

We started with the Drums of Heaven and Chicken Wontons — crispy, juicy, and packed with flavor. The real showstopper, though, was the Murg Kheema Mutter with Cheese Chilli Naan — a fusion that somehow feels both nostalgic and refreshingly new. Pair that with their signature cocktail, Amber of Dunes, and you’ve got yourself a match made in foodie heaven. Don’t leave without digging into the Fudge Mountain Melt — it’s rich, gooey, and everything a dessert should be.

Osttaad doesn’t just serve food — it tells stories through spice, texture, and legacy. Perfect for a date night, family dinner, or even a solo soul-food session, it’s a must-visit for anyone looking to experience something truly special in Mumbai’s dining scene.

Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Great Vibe and Food, But Don't Waste Your Money on the Drinks
​
The Good:
I’ll start with the positives—the general ambience of Series A Bar and Grill is actually very good. It’s got a nice setup, and the frontline staff working behind the bar are friendly, polite, and do their best.
​
The Bad:
Unfortunately, the actual service and product quality completely ruin the experience. If you are going there to drink, consider this a warning: beware when ordering cocktails. The alcohol content in them is practically non-existent; you can't even taste a hint of spirit. It felt like paying premium prices for overpriced juice.

​To make matters worse, it takes an absolute eternity for drinks to actually arrive at your table. When we tried to address the delays and quality, it became painfully obvious that the upstairs bar manager is completely clueless and unable to run a smooth operation.

​Final Verdict
​A cool atmosphere can only carry a place so far. When a bar can't get its drinks or service right, it's a major red flag. I would highly suggest you find an alternative place in Santacruz to spend your hard-earned money.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Avatara for dinner to celebrate our 19th wedding anniversary, and it was an exceptional experience from start to finish. Their thoughtfully curated 16-course menu, inspired by the Indus Valley and complemented by traditional regional flavors from across India, was truly unique and memorable.
Every course—from the appetizers to the mains and desserts and also Paan ... was beautifully presented and expertly explained by Anirudh, whose warm hospitality added greatly to the evening. Every dish had a surprise twist to it.
We were also surprised with a lovely cake for our anniversary celebration, which made the occasion even more special.
Avatara offers a true gastronomic journey, and I would highly recommend it to anyone who appreciates innovative vegetarian cuisine. A must-visit for food lovers.

We ordered the 16 course menu with wine pairing. Food arrived promptly and the waiters explained each dish and the respective pairings well. The dishes were very thoughtful and creative, adding to the eating experience. Every dish hit the spot.

featured_reviews.name: Stanley Vaz
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Avatara, one does not merely dine—one participates in a carefully orchestrated culinary narrative that challenges every preconceived notion of vegetarian cuisine.

From the moment you are seated, the service establishes its quiet authority: attentive without intrusion, polished without pretension. Among the team, Viraj stands out—not with flamboyance, but with a rare, intuitive finesse. His understanding of the menu is not rehearsed, but lived; each course arrives not just as food, but as a story, delivered with precision and warmth.

The cuisine itself is nothing short of revelatory. In a world where vegetarian fare is often relegated to the periphery, Avatara asserts dominance. Every plate is a study in balance—texture, temperature, acidity, and depth all meticulously calibrated. Ingredients are elevated beyond their humble origins, transformed into expressions that are both rooted and avant-garde.

What distinguishes Avatara is its restraint. There is no unnecessary theatrics, no overindulgence in molecular excess. Instead, the kitchen demonstrates confidence—allowing flavours to speak, yet ensuring each bite leaves a lasting impression. It is this quiet mastery that aligns the restaurant with the philosophy of Michelin-starred establishments.

In its totality, Avatara delivers an experience that is immersive, thoughtful, and deeply satisfying. It is not simply one of the finest vegetarian meals—it is one of the finest meals, period.

featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Harish Lunch Home for a non-veg dinner, and I have to say, my experience was quite mixed. While the restaurant does have a parking facility and offers both bar and family seating sections, the food and service left much to be desired.
This place is known for its seafood and bar setup, so I had some expectations going in. We ordered a variety of dishes:
•	Manchow Soup
•	Chicken Ghee Roast
•	Butter Garlic Prawns
•	Bombil Fry
•	Chicken Crispy
•	Egg Fried Rice

Out of everything, only the soup was passable. The chicken ghee roast was underwhelming—the masala wasn’t cooked properly. Butter garlic prawns lacked flavor and freshness, and the bombil fry didn’t meet the usual seafood standard either.

The chicken crispy was the biggest disappointment. It was hard and chewy, nowhere near the crispy texture we expected—it honestly ruined the mood of the meal.

For the main course, we ordered egg fried rice, but the waiter failed to guide us properly with portion sizes, especially considering we were a big family. This led to a shortage and overall dining discomfort.

In short, service was poor, food was mostly below average, and portion sizes were not family-friendly.
I would not recommend this place for a proper family dinner. If you’re looking for quality food and attentive service, I suggest you explore other options.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

Experience the true flavors of Malvani home-cooked meals at "Aaplo Kokan" – a paradise for food lovers!

featured_reviews.name: THE SIMPLE SOUL
featured_reviews.review_text:
A jewel worth your moolah! Nestled in the by-lanes of Borivali, this little gem is a sparkler, for sure. Your search for authentic Malvani cuisine ends here.
Be it the use of spices, the freshness of the ingredients, the quantity, the quality and the authenticity...all scream 'Fantastic'!
The thalis are delicious and freshly prepared. They do not scrimp on the fried fish or prawns. In fact, on offer, is a free side of freshly fried bombils with the fish thalis and free kothimbir wadi with the Veg thali on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
The fish is fresh. The solkadi is yummy. The JOWARI BHAKRI is super soft..😋
The Kothimbir wadis are delightful too.
The fish gravy is a tad spicy...not for the faint-hearted. But just the way Malvani cuisine should be.
The fresh lime soda is decent.
The absolute highlight: The modaks, though it was a 20 minute wait.  Fresh. Authentic. Mouth-watering, to say the least. And the drizzle of ghee over the modaks...👌😋😋...oohhlaalaa..next level. A++
The juiciest, most scrumptious modaks you could ever have  eaten.
Definitely worth a return...over and over. If consistency prevails.
Thumbs up!! 👍👌

featured_reviews.name: Mamta Sarvankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
You must visit  Aaplo Konkan for their incredible service and authentic Malvani seafood. I previously visited Mazghar, but in my opinion, the taste here is far superior and much more delicious.
​The food is extremely flavorful, especially the fish dishes which capture the true essence of Malvani cuisine. The best part is the pricing—it is very reasonable. Highly recommended for seafood lovers..

featured_reviews.name: Sanket Lad
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover then you shouldn’t miss this amazing place in Borivali west named Aaplo Kokan

Authentic Kokani and Malvani Cuisines with great quality as well as quantity.

The owner as well as staff is really friendly and welcoming.

We tried their halwa mini thali which was a perfect lunch/dinner meal to have one.

There highly recommended all in one thali has my heart as it includes all of the main seafood items that you must try like crab curry, surmai fry, prawns fry, jawla,tisrya sukha,bhakri,rice & solkadi.

The place has indoor and outdoor seating with full on konkan vibe in it.

Do visit this place.

Also they are running one offer on every Tuesday Wednesday Thursday on any full thali you will get bombil fry absolutely free!!

And they have also started free home delivery services in Borivali on order above 500.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Hemmady
featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Akash Kargutkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Extremely disappointing experience. For a place claiming to serve Maharashtrian cuisine, the flavors were completely missing—bland and unauthentic. featured_reviews.name: Smith Sirvel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am extremely disappointed with my recent order from JP’s Lunch Home. I had ordered mutton gravy expecting a proper dish with meat, but what I received was just plain gravy with absolutely no mutton pieces in it.

This is not a minor mistake—the main component of the dish was completely missing. It feels misleading to charge customers for a mutton dish and deliver something that doesn’t even contain mutton.

What makes it worse is the inconvenience caused. I was left without a proper meal and had to go through the hassle of raising a complaint and following up for resolution. This is not the level of service one expects when ordering from a listed restaurant.

Restaurants need to take basic quality checks seriously before dispatching orders. Sending out incomplete items reflects very poorly on both the restaurant and the delivery platform.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and necessary action is taken so that other customers do not face the same issue.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik P
featured_reviews.review_text:
**Absolutely disgraceful and humiliating experience**
This was not just bad service, this was outright insulting behavior by your staff.
A waiter named “Anna” displayed shocking levels of arrogance, rudeness and complete lack of basic etiquette. Our order was delayed by over 30 minutes and despite asking multiple times, we were blatantly ignored. When he finally chose to respond, it was with a careless and rude excuse about oil being refilled, as if customers are expected to tolerate such delays without communication.
What happened next was even worse.
When the food arrived my wife noticed that the halwa portion served was not even a spoonful, which is unacceptable. Another staff member showing basic common sense and courtesy, provided an extra serving as a goodwill gesture.
But then, in an act that was deeply disrespectful and outright shocking, this same waiter “Anna” walked up to our table and snatched the extra serving directly from our plate without even asking us, questioning why it was given.
This was extremely humiliating, especially in front of others. My wife felt insulted and we had to explicitly ask him to stay away from our table.
Let me be very clear, this is not a small mistake. This reflects complete failure in staff training, customer respect and management oversight.
We chose not to create a scene there, but this experience has ensured we will never return.
If this is the standard of service you tolerate, customers should think twice before visiting.
Train your staff or replace them because this level of behavior is unacceptable.
**Very very poor experience given by JP and your staff "Anna"**

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.
